chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) he said: I was narrated by Muhammad ibn Abd al-Mu'min, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever visits the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of 'Arafah, Allah will record for him one million pilgrimages with the Awaited Imam (peace be upon him), and one million pilgrimages with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the freeing of one million souls, and one million mounts of horses in the cause of Allah. And Allah, Exalted and Glorious, will call him 'My truthful servant', he believed in My promise. And the angels will say: 'So-and-so is truthful, Allah purified him from above His Throne,' and he will be called on earth 'Cherub'.
ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for visiting Imam Husayn's grave on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith underscores the unique merit of Ziyarat al-Husayn on the Day of 'Arafah, linking the Imam’s shrine to the sanctity of the Prophet’s pilgrimage. It promises extraordinary rewards, including the manumission of a thousand slaves and the unique angelic title 'Karubiyya,' reflecting a high station of divine proximity and truthfulness (Sidq) recognized by both Allah and the angels.
